sam: Quick summary — I ran a hybrid benchmark (trace-replay + synthetic trace synthesis) to isolate kernel-selection flips during continuous batching. Found a reproducible p99 regression when KV cache miss rate crosses ~18%.

jia: Can you drop the harness + config you used?

sam: Sure, config snippet below (minimal):
```
harness: hybrid-replay
replay_trace: traces/2026-02-11/customer-A.json
synth_profile: token_len_dist=prod-7d
batching: {max_batch_size: 256, max_delay_ms: 8, continuous: true, per_tenant_batchcap: dynamic}
kvcache: {ttl_ms: 60000, prefetch: true}
kernel_selector: {policy: latency_cost, penalty_on_swap_ms: 2}
```

marta: Interesting. What metrics jumped?

sam: Key diffs:
- p50 stable (~28ms)
- p95 +8%
- p99 +12% when miss rate >18%
- kernel swap count up 3x (hotpath switches from matmul-opt to fallback kernel)
- KV cache hit rate dropped from 84% -> 67% under synthetic microbursts

leo: Did you control for sequence-length distribution? That can change kernel choice.

sam: Yes — the synth_profile matches prod 7-day seq histogram; replay alone undersamples short bursts so it underestimates swapping. Hybrid gives both realism and stress.

alex: Can you paste the profiling flame result? Even coarse top functions is fine.

sam: Paste of top 6 stacks (relative time):
```
1) attention_kv_lookup (32%)
2) matmul_fast (18%)
3) fallback_matmul (15%)
4) kv_cache_eviction (8%)
5) kernel_selector.evaluate (7%)
6) cuda_sync_wait (6%)
```

marta: So fallback_matmul and evictions correlate. Do you see per-tenant skew?

sam: Yes — tenant B (heavy short-chat) causes many small batches -> increases eviction churn for shared KV and triggers kernel selector to prefer fallback kernel that tolerates jitter. Tenant B's continuous batching keeps batch sizes low but increases request rate => more overhead.

jia: Proposed methodology to be apples-to-apples:
1) Use identical seq-length and arrival CDF across synth and replay (we synthesize arrival jitter onto replay timestamps).
2) Force same initial KV cache warmup window (60s).
3) Run paired experiments back-to-back on same machine image and kernel build.
4) Collect: per-request kernel_id, batch_size, kv_hit, p50/p95/p99, cpu/gpu_util, kernel_swap_ts.

leo: Add: pin model_version and quantization flags. Also capture GPU clock and mem pressure.

sam: Agreed. I also added an experiment sweep: vary per_tenant_batchcap = [32,64,128,256] and max_delay_ms = [2,4,8,16] and record fairness index (Jain) on p95 between tenants.

marta: Early results from that sweep?

sam: Quick table (high level):
- batchcap 32 / delay 2ms -> p95 tenants: [38, 42, 120] ms -> Jain=0.54 (bad fairness)
- batchcap 128 / delay 8ms -> p95: [30, 32, 36] ms -> Jain=0.96 (good)
- batchcap 256 / delay 16ms -> p95: [28, 30, 35] ms -> Jain=0.93
- batchcap dynamic / delay 8ms -> p95: [31, 90, 33] ms -> Jain=0.64 (tenant B starved occasionally)

marta: So dynamic per-tenant growth without constraints hurts fairness. Good catch.

alex: For the kernel selection regression — what's the decision surface? Is it batch_size x seq_len x mem_pressure?

sam: From classifier logs, primary features were batch_size and avg_seq_len; secondary was recent_eviction_rate (window 5s). If eviction_rate > 0.15 it biases to fallback. That lines up with KV churn threshold.

jia: Action items:
- (sam) publish exact harness + seed to bench repo and attach raw traces (due EOD tomorrow).
- (leo) add GPU mem pressure telemetry into bench collector (due 48h).
- (marta) run targeted tenant-isolation run with tenant B pinned to dedicated pool (to confirm shared-KV hypothesis) (due Mon).
- (alex) draft kernel-selector tweak: add hysteresis on swap and prefer stable kernel for short bursts if swap_count>2 in 10s (PR proposal) (due Wed).

sam: I've pushed a small synthetic harness flag: --synth-jitter=poisson-lambda=0.02 and seed to replicate the microbursts. Example run command:
```
./benchctl run --config hybrid.yaml --repeat 3 --out results/hybrid-2141598765
```

leo: CI bot can we gate that job on the same GPU image? @ci-bot any ideas for labeling nodes?

ci-bot: You can use label gpu:perf-rt-v3 to get the same image. I've queued a build with the harness collector enabled.

marta: One more thing — let's record kernel selector confidence and add a metric kernel_swap_penalty_ms to better attribute p99 jumps to swap overhead vs native kernel slowness.

sam: Good call. I'll augment the collector. Also adding a small log line in runtime: "kernel_swap -> from=%s to=%s reason=%s" to make timestamps match metrics.

jia: This thread is great. After runs, we'll convert to a short benchmark protocol doc and add to eng-runtime bench-playbook. Keep notes concise. :thumbsup:

sam: Will do. Uploading harness and sample output soon.
